all.text: At this latitude, the Earth's spin carries the ship east at about 790 mph, whatever the captain is doing.
The sun reaches its highest point here about 43 minutes after it does in Southampton.
Drill straight through the Earth from here and you'd surface at 40.3°S, 167.7°E, about 540 km from Christchurch.
This far north, they're roughly level with Beijing, even though it's a world away.
The seabed is roughly 5,282 m below the ship, which is about 16.0 Eiffel Towers stacked up.
